scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

While it's wonderful that you find guidance and comfort in the wisdom of centuries, it's also important to consider how this approach might influence your sense of agency and autonomy. On one hand, drawing upon the collective wisdom of tradition can provide a sense of stability, continuity, and connection to a larger community. By considering the interpretations and insights of respected rabbis and scholars, you may feel more confident in your decisions, knowing that they are grounded in a rich and time-tested heritage. On the other hand, relying too heavily on tradition might lead to a sense of disconnection from your own thoughts, feelings, and values. If you consistently prioritize the opinions of others over your own instincts, you may start to feel like you're not truly making your own decisions. This could lead to a sense of disempowerment or a lack of personal ownership over your choices. It's possible that, in some cases, you might feel like you're simply following a predetermined path, rather than forging your own way. This could be particularly true if you're not taking the time to reflect on your own values, goals, and motivations, and instead, are primarily relying on external authorities to guide your decision-making. However, it's also important to note that tradition and personal autonomy are not mutually exclusive. In fact, many Jewish scholars and rabbis would argue that the study of Torah and tradition is meant to inform and enrich one's own decision-making, rather than replace it. By engaging with the wisdom of the past, you can develop a deeper understanding of the world and your place in it, which can, in turn, inform your own values and decision-making. Ultimately, the key is to find a balance between respecting tradition and honoring your own inner voice. It might be helpful to ask yourself questions like: What are my own values and goals? How do they align with the traditions and interpretations I'm drawing upon? Am I using tradition as a source of guidance, or am I relying on it as a crutch?
